task: Add a read-only command `python -m incident_commander alerts` listing the simulated alerts (id and identifying facts), no state change, no env vars, purity gate passing, unit tests, README command list.

input.question: what do the project rules and structure require for this task?

output.found: CLI is incident_commander/__main__.py (argparse subcommands tools/investigate/gates/run). Alerts are frozen dataclasses (alert_id, service, fired_at, severity, metric, summary) in fixtures/alerts.py, reachable via SimWorld().alert_ids()/alert(). Output style is key=value lines via report.kv. README has a Commands list. Baseline: dod purity PASS, scikit-learn 1.8.0 importable. Tests are unittest, CLI tests run subprocesses in tests/test_cli.py.
constraints: incident_commander imports stdlib+sklearn only, no env vars, never imports ic_plus
decisions use typed evidence only, never severity (listing only displays it)
tests ship with code, unittest not pytest
never push; commit on the existing branch, Conventional Commits with body

input.command: python -m incident_commander.dod purity; python -m unittest discover -s tests (baseline, before changes)

output.result: purity PASS (22 modules); 201 tests OK; ruff 0.17.0 available; scikit-learn 1.8.0 importable

input.question: What output format should the alerts command use?

output.decision: One key=value line per alert using report.kv, in world order, plus an M-free plain header-less listing: alert=ALRT-9001 service=checkout-service severity_label=high metric=latency_ms fired_at=1760000100 summary="...".
output.why: The existing tools command already prints alert=.. service=.. fired_at=.. severity_label=.. via kv; reusing kv keeps output deterministic and greppable and consistent with the project trace contract. severity is called severity_label there because it is only a label, never evidence.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: no table helper exists; wide summary text breaks alignment; harder to parse
scope creep; project has no JSON output anywhere

assumptions: fired_at as a raw epoch number is acceptable, matching tools output
risks: Future format change breaks scripts; tests pin the shape

input.question: Where should the data come from, and how to guarantee read-only?

output.decision: Read alerts through SimWorld().alert_ids() and .alert(id) (the same accessors other commands use) and do not call any tool, clock, executor or apply_remediation. Add cmd_alerts() in __main__.py and a test that the world is unchanged.
output.why: world.py is the single access path; fixtures/alerts.py says it is the only place incident ids exist, so I do not duplicate ids. Using SimWorld is read-only since only apply_remediation mutates.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: bypasses SimWorld, which other commands go through

assumptions: SimWorld construction has no side effects (it is used by every other command)
risks: none for state; tests will assert equality with ALERTS

input.question: Which fields to show and what to do about the summary text?

output.decision: Show id, service, severity_label, metric, fired_at, and summary (quoted by fmt). No invented data (no status, owner).
output.why: Those are all six fields the Alert type stores. Summary is fixture text authored by the project, not log text, so it is not untrusted content; log text is the thing the project hides.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: it is stored identifying info and short
would need new formatting code and a timezone choice; raw epoch matches the tools command

risks: a future alert with a quote in the summary would be printed unescaped by fmt (existing behaviour)

input.goal: add cmd_alerts and wire the alerts subcommand

output.summary: Added cmd_alerts() printing one kv line per alert from SimWorld, an argparse subparser `alerts` with no arguments, dispatch in main(), and updated the module docstring.

input.question: How to test the command, given the world is rebuilt inside the command?

output.decision: New file tests/test_alerts_command.py: in-process main() with captured stdout for content/order/determinism/extra-arg rejection, plus one subprocess run with only PATH and SYSTEMROOT in the environment.
output.why: Project tests put CLI tests in subprocesses but a separate small file keeps test_cli.py untouched (rules: minimal edits, small files); in-process is faster and lets me capture argparse exit. The subprocess test proves no env vars are needed.
assumptions: python needs PATH/SYSTEMROOT on Windows only
risks: the no-state-change test is weak: cmd_alerts builds its own SimWorld, so I can only check the fixture table and a separate world are unchanged, not the command internal world; read-only-ness rests on the code calling no mutating method

output.result: 6 tests OK; module under test is the clone code (python run with the clone as cwd, alerts output matched fixtures in the clone)

input.command: python -m unittest discover -s tests; python -m ruff check .; python -m ruff format --check .; python -m incident_commander.dod purity

output.result: 207 tests OK (201 before); ruff check passed; format check 59 files already formatted; G1 purity PASS 22 modules (the alerts command adds no import)

input.question: Which docs to update and what not to touch?

output.decision: Added one line to the README Commands list and one entry in memory-bank/progress.md; did not edit CHANGELOG.md or traces/, did not mark a roadmap version.
output.why: CLAUDE.md says generated files are never hand-edited and progress.md is updated at session end; the command is not a roadmap milestone.

alternatives_considered.rejected_because: it describes the milestone focus (v0.5), unchanged by this side feature

risks: progress.md entry sits outside the version list format

input.question: what should the next person know?

output.notes: The command prints raw epoch fired_at like the tools command; no human-readable time. CHANGELOG not regenerated (no generator installed per memory bank). I did not run the full CI or the other dod gates (only purity exists). Python used was the system python (scikit-learn 1.8.0), not the project 3.12 venv. The unchanged-state test is indirect. Branch not pushed or merged.
